text: Most online polls ask you to trust whoever runs them. They can quietly change the count, and you would never know.
Ballot is different. It's a voting app built on Ethereum, where every poll and every vote is recorded on a public blockchain.
These boxes are live blocks from the chain. The green ones hold Ballot votes and polls, happening right now.
Here's how it works, from start to finish.
First, connect a wallet, like MetaMask. There's no sign up and no password. Your wallet is your identity.
Now, let's create a poll. Type your question.
Add between two and ten options.
And pick a deadline, anywhere from five minutes to thirty days.
The counters show bytes, not letters, because that's exactly how the smart contract measures them.
Before you sign, Ballot shows you a review. A poll is permanent. Once it's on the chain, nobody can edit it, not even us.
Sign it, and within seconds, the poll is live for everyone.
Other members are already voting. Let's cast ours.
Before your wallet even opens, the app rehearses the vote, so mistakes are caught early, and for free.
Checked, signed, broadcast, recorded. And here's the best part: your ballot receipt.
It shows the transaction, the block, and the exact time. It's read back from the blockchain itself, so it's proof, not a promise. Anyone can check it on Etherscan.
Try to vote twice, and the contract simply says no. One wallet, one vote.
Results update live, with a count and a percentage for every option.
When the deadline passes, the poll closes by itself, using blockchain time, and the winner is declared.
The results page gathers every poll, live and final. Anyone can view it, even without a wallet.
And My votes keeps track of every poll you've taken part in.
No admin. No hidden database. No way to change a vote. Just open, verifiable voting.
Ballot. Every vote, provable.
